meta.title: JushoAI - Fill Japanese forms into the right fields
meta.description: A Chromium browser extension that fills Japanese web forms (split names, furigana, split addresses) in one click. Rules first, AI as a helper, and a preview before anything is entered.

footer.tagline: Japanese forms, filled the right way.

hero.eyebrow: Available on the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons and Firefox Add-ons
hero.titleBefore: Names, furigana and addresses on Japanese forms,
hero.titleEmphasis: in the right fields and the right format
hero.tagline: Forms split into family name, given name, furigana and prefecture-to-street fields get filled in one click. You review everything in a preview first.

features.title: Built for what makes Japanese forms hard

items.title: Handles split fields as they are
items.body: Fills split family/given names, furigana, postal code, phone number and prefecture-to-building address fields in the shape each field expects.

items.title: Rules first, AI as a helper
items.body: Fields are classified by rules first; only the ambiguous ones are classified by the AI you configure. The values themselves are produced by fixed logic.

items.title: Review in a preview before filling
items.body: See the list of fields and values before anything is entered. Fields that already have a value are never overwritten.

items.title: Multiple profiles and addresses
items.body: Keep up to 10 profiles and up to 10 addresses. Each address can be tied to the profile that uses it. The toolbar icon shows what is registered and which profile is in use.

items.title: Designed to keep your profile values local
items.body: Your profile values are never sent anywhere. When you configure an AI provider, only field metadata (name, label and the like) is sent.

items.title: The button stays out of the way
items.body: The `JushoAI で入力` button appears where it does not overlap any fields. If it still gets in the way, drag it somewhere clear. Its translucent background keeps the field underneath readable.

mock.uiNote: The extension's interface is in Japanese.
mock.captionButton: A "JushoAI で入力" (fill with JushoAI) button appears next to the form. The badge shows the AI status.
mock.captionPreview: Review fields and values before filling. Fields classified by the AI carry an "AI判定" (AI) mark.
mock.captionGuide: Click the badge to open a guide that explains the status and what to do.
mock.captionForm: Split fields receive values in the shape each field expects.

demo.title: See it in action
demo.lead: A two-minute demo. It shows the flow from reviewing the preview to filling a form, on real screens.

items.title: Register
items.body: In the settings page, register your name, furigana, email, phone number and addresses. You can register several addresses.

items.title: Press the button
items.body: Press "JushoAI で入力" that appears near the form.

items.title: Review the preview
items.body: Check the list of fields and values. If you registered several addresses, pick one here.

items.title: Fill
items.body: Press 入力する (fill) and only the fields you reviewed are filled.

items.title: Names
items.body: Works with separate family and given name fields or a single field. For a single field it reads the field's example text to decide whether to put a space between them.

items.title: Furigana
items.body: Supports full-width katakana, hiragana and half-width katakana, converting to match the field's example text or description.

items.title: Addresses
items.body: Supports addresses split across fields such as prefecture, city, street and building. Prefecture dropdowns are matched even when the notation differs, such as 東京 versus 東京都.

items.title: Phone and postal code
items.body: Handles hyphenated and plain numbers, in a single field or split fields, judged from the field's example text and maximum length.

items.title: Birthday, gender, age group and school
items.body: The birthday is entered as year, month, day or era. Gender and age group go into dropdowns and radio buttons, and the school and department into matching fields.

items.title: Safe filling
items.body: Fields that already have a value are not overwritten, and values longer than the maximum length are not entered but flagged.

providers.title: AI, only when you want it
providers.lead: The default is "off". Choose a provider in the settings page only if you want AI to help with fields the rules cannot decide.

items.name: OpenAI-compatible API
items.body: Presets for OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, Ollama and LM Studio. Enter the base URL, model name and API key.

items.name: Google Gemini
items.body: Enter the model name and API key.

items.name: Built-in browser AI
items.body: Chrome (Gemini Nano) or Edge (Phi-mini). Needs a flag and a restart, and nothing leaves your device.

safety.title: How we keep it safe
safety.lead: JushoAI handles personal information, so it is built on three rules: never fill without asking, never send without being asked, and layer the defenses.

items.title: Nothing is filled until you approve
items.body: Pressing the button does not fill anything. Only the fields you confirm in the preview and approve with the fill button are filled. There is no auto-fill on page load.

items.title: No overwriting, no truncating
items.body: Fields that already have a value are never overwritten. A value longer than the field's maximum length is not truncated; it is skipped with a warning. Read-only and disabled fields are skipped too.

items.title: Undo after filling
items.body: Right after filling, the undo button restores only the fields JushoAI filled to their previous state. Fields you typed into afterwards are left alone. The history lives only in memory on your device and is never saved or sent.

items.title: Rules make the values, AI only classifies
items.body: AI only classifies what kind of field it is; it never produces the values. Your profile values are not given to AI or to anyone else. AI is off by default.

items.title: Strict checks on the destination
items.body: https only (http only for localhost and similar). Internal network addresses are rejected, and DNS results are checked when you save and again just before each call. Redirects are not followed. A new destination receives nothing until you have reviewed its IP addresses and approved it.

items.title: Minimal keys and permissions
items.body: API keys are stored encrypted with AES-GCM and are never shown on the settings page. Network permission is not requested at install; only the saved provider's host is requested, when you save.

items.title: UI the page cannot touch
items.body: The extension's UI sits inside a closed Shadow DOM that page scripts cannot reach. Strings that come from the page are shown as text, never interpreted as HTML.

items.title: A local record of every call
items.body: Every AI call is recorded in an audit log on your device. You can review, download or delete it on the settings page. Entries disappear automatically after 7 days.

items.title: Only field metadata is sent
items.body: If you configure an AI provider, the name, label, placeholder, nearby heading, type and maxlength of fields are sent to it. Your profile values and values already in fields are not. Labels and headings are text shown on the page, so personal information visible on the page can be part of what is sent.

items.title: Network only on click
items.body: Merely opening a page never contacts an AI provider.

items.title: API keys are stored encrypted
items.body: Leaked storage alone cannot decrypt them. The extension's own code can still read them.

install.title: Install
steps: In Chrome, install from the Chrome Web Store. In Edge, install from Edge Add-ons. In Firefox, install from Firefox Add-ons (AMO).
To load a zip instead, unzip the release from GitHub Releases. In Firefox, load it as a temporary add-on from about:debugging (it is removed when Firefox quits).

To load the zip in Chrome or Edge instead, open chrome://extensions or edge://extensions, turn on Developer mode, and choose "Load unpacked" to select the unzipped folder (the label may differ by browser).
In the extension's settings page, register your profile and addresses.
install.store: Install from the Chrome Web Store
install.more: See the "Getting started" guide for details.

faq.title: FAQ

items.a: Yes. Fields are classified by rules, and AI only helps with ambiguous ones. AI is off by default.
Nothing, unless you configure AI. If you do, only field metadata is sent; your profile values and the values already in fields are not.
You review everything in a preview before filling, and fields that already have a value are not overwritten. Right after filling, you can undo.

items.q: What do you do for safety?
items.a: Preview approval, no overwriting, undo, never giving profile values to AI, destination checks with first-use approval, encrypted API keys and an audit log of every call. See How we keep it safe on the home page and the Safety guide.

items.q: Does it work on every form?
items.a: It handles common inputs (text, email, tel, and prefecture dropdowns). Fields it cannot classify are left alone.
Allow the extension's origin (chrome-extension:// followed by the extension ID) in Ollama's OLLAMA_ORIGINS setting.

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.lead: Feature requests, forms that did not fill correctly, and bug reports are welcome as GitHub issues. The buttons below open a ready-made form (a GitHub account is required).

items.title: Feature request
items.body: Tell us about a feature you would like, or something that is hard to use.

items.title: A form that did not fill
items.body: Send the URL of the form and what happened.

items.title: Bug report
items.body: If something misbehaves, tell us how to reproduce it.

feedback.note: Issues are public. Do not include personal information such as your name, address or phone number.
